newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Former Viet Cong leader Nguyen Huu Tho dies at 86.
newsitem.headline: Former Viet Cong leader Nguyen Huu Tho dies at 86.

text.p: Nguyen Huu Tho, a French-educated Saigon lawyer and former leader of Hanoi's National Liberation Front (NLF), has died after a long illness, the official Communist Party daily Nhan Dan said on Friday. He was 86.

"He was a patriotic intellectual lawyer, he carried out revolutionary activities for more than 50 years and made many great contributions to the revolutionary cause of our party and our people," Nhan Dan said in a black-bordered tribute.
The paper said there would be a state funeral for Tho, who died in Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, on Tuesday.

Tho graduated from Aix-en-Provence law school in 1932. Eighteen years later he took part in a Saigon demonstration against French colonial rule and American interference in Vietnam, after which he was arrested and jailed until 1952.

In 1954, after the defeat of France's forces at Dien Bien Phu, Tho became vice-chairman of a group demanding strict implementation of the Geneva Accord, which ended hostilities and provided for the release of prisoners.
He was arrested by the South Vietnam authorities again in 1954 and remained in prison until 1961, after which he became chairman of the central committee of the NLF.

The NLF, whose platform called for neutralisation of Vietnam, the withdrawal of all foreign troops and gradual reunification, was known as the Viet Cong during the ensuing war against the Americans and U.S.-backed Saigon forces.
After the war, which ended in 1975, Tho became a member of reunified Vietnam's National Assembly, then the country's Vice President and, in 1980, Acting President.
